title: Davisson Offset Limit — Pile Failure Criterion

s_failure.description: Settlement at which pile is considered to have reached ultimate capacity

applicability: Most widely used in North America for driven piles. Plot the offset line on the load-settlement curve starting at s = 3.8 + D/120 with slope 1/(AE/L). Capacity = load at intersection with measured curve. Not recommended for large-diameter drilled shafts — use 5% D criterion instead.

title: Chin-Kondner Hyperbolic Extrapolation
equation: Q_ult = 1 / slope of (Δ/Q vs. Δ) linear portion
applicability: Plot Δ/Q on y-axis vs. Δ on x-axis. After initial nonlinear zone, data falls on a straight line with slope m. Q_ult = 1/m. Typically overpredicts capacity by 20–40% — apply correction factor of 0.80. Useful when test not taken to full failure.

title: FHWA 5% Diameter Criterion (Drilled Shafts)
equation: Q_ult = load at settlement of 0.05 × D
applicability: For drilled shafts and large-diameter piles where Davisson criterion is too conservative (Davisson offset becomes very large, requiring excessive settlement to reach). A 1.0 m shaft: failure at 50 mm settlement. Simple and rational for large-diameter elements.

title: Pile Elastic Compression

Δ_elastic.description: Elastic shortening of pile under load P

L.description: Pile length (or effective length considering load transfer)

E.description: Elastic modulus (steel: 200 GPa, concrete: 25–35 GPa, timber: 10–14 GPa)

applicability: For uniform pile with load applied at top and resisted at toe. In reality, shaft friction reduces load progressively — effective length for elastic compression is < L. Approximate: use L/2 if shaft friction dominant, L if end bearing dominant.

title: CASE Method — Dynamic Capacity (Simplified)

F₁, V₁.description: Force and velocity at pile head at time of impact peak (t₁)

F₂, V₂.description: Force and velocity at time t₂ = t₁ + 2L/c

c.description: Wave speed in pile (5120 m/s steel, 3000–4000 m/s concrete)

applicability: Simplified dynamic capacity. Static capacity: R_static = R_total - J_c × (F₁ + Z×V₁ - R_total) where J_c = CASE damping factor (0.1–0.9 depending on soil type). CAPWAP signal matching provides more refined result.

title: Pile Impedance

Z.description: Pile impedance (relates force to velocity in wave propagation)

applicability: Fundamental parameter for dynamic pile testing. For a uniform pile: F = Z × V for a downward traveling wave. Changes in impedance (cross-section change, crack, soil inclusion) cause wave reflections used in integrity testing.

title: Anchor Elastic Elongation (Expected Free Length Verification)

Δ_elastic.description: Theoretical elastic elongation of the unbonded (free) length

A_t.description: Cross-sectional area of tendon (total strand area)

E_s.description: Modulus of elasticity of tendon (195 GPa for strand, 200 GPa for bar)

applicability: Measured elastic movement must be ≥ 80% of theoretical for L_free and ≤ theoretical for L_free + L_bond (full tendon length). This verification ensures the bond zone is holding and the free length is unbonded. If measured elongation < 80% of theoretical free length: possible short free length, bond zone too close to wall, or anchor debonding.

title: Creep Rate for Anchor Acceptance

creep_rate.description: Creep rate (movement per log cycle of time)

Δ₁, Δ₂.description: Anchor head movements at times t₁ and t₂

t₁, t₂.description: Start and end times of observation (typically 1 min and 10 min)

applicability: At maximum test load hold: creep rate must be < 2 mm/log cycle for most soil anchors, < 1 mm for rock anchors (varies by specification). If exceeded: extend hold time. If still exceeded: anchor may need regrouting, redesign, or replacement.

title: Modulus of Subgrade Reaction from Plate Load Test
applicability: Typically reported at s = 1.27 mm (0.05 in) for pavement design. k_s is stress-dependent (nonlinear) — report at the design stress level. Size correction for footing design: k_footing = k_plate × (B_plate / B_footing) for granular soils; k_footing ≈ k_plate for clays.

title: Statnamic Unloading Point Method
applicability: At the unloading point (v = 0, a ≈ 0 at maximum displacement), F_static ≈ F_statnamic directly. For the full curve, the damping term c×v must be estimated. Method assumes rate-dependent resistance is viscous. Correction factors (0.90–0.95) may apply for clay soils.
